name: Montview Flats
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: South Metro Housing Options, Littleton's housing authority, built Montview Flats, a 50-unit, four-story family building at 5848 S. Rapp St. in downtown Littleton for households at 30% to 70% AMI, with a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award from CHFA; it held its grand opening on 2026-06-30.
why_it_matters: It is a finished example of a housing authority using a city inclusionary housing ordinance (fee-in-lieu money plus parking and density relief) on a 0.69-acre infill site, stacked with 9% credits, ARPA, CDBG and Division of Housing gap money, and opening about 11 months after groundbreaking.

status.label: Open: grand opening 2026-06-30; leasing under way
status.detail: Groundbreaking was held on 2025-07-30 and the grand opening on 2026-06-30, per the Littleton Independent. SMHO's property page says the building opened in 2026, is taking applications and offers a first-month-free move-in special. Occupancy level and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not public.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and SMHO board materials reporting occupancy.

key_numbers.meaning: All income-restricted at 30% to 70% AMI; 30 units at or below 50% AMI; 8 units carry SMHO project-based vouchers.

key_numbers.value: $1,352,727 a year in federal 9% credit plus $700,000 of state credit
key_numbers.meaning: About $13.5M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred). The applicant had requested $1,450,000 a year.
Reported at the 2026 opening, about $513,000 per unit (inferred); SMHO gave $26.6M at the 2025 groundbreaking.
Including Littleton inclusionary housing fees ($900,000), Littleton ARPA funds, Arapahoe County CDBG ($300,000), Centennial, the Division of Housing and an SMHO carryback loan.

background.text: Littleton's inclusionary housing ordinance, passed unanimously in November 2022, made the project possible: it requires 5% affordable units or a fee-in-lieu from developments of five or more units, and gives affordable projects fee rebates and relief from parking, density and lot-size rules. Montview Flats used that relief and $900,000 of the fee money.

SMHO's first 9% deal in 30 years was Overlook at Powers Park (51 senior units, completed January 2024) with Metro West Housing Solutions; for Montview Flats SMHO took the lead role and reused the Overlook architect, contractor and financial consultant.

Environmental: the Phase I prompted a limited Phase II, with a CDPHE-accepted mitigation plan; a 69-decibel noise level (above HUD's 65 dB action level) required wall assemblies that bring interior noise to 45 dB or less.

Cost drivers named by the applicant: hydrodynamic separators and an underground detention vault because the streets have no storm sewer, plus downtown zoning rules on articulation, massing and exterior materials.
Market study figures in the application: 5.3% overall capture rate (7.3% including projects under construction) and 4.8% market-area vacancy in the third quarter of 2023.

Construction took about 11 months from the 2025-07-30 groundbreaking to the 2026-06-30 grand opening; at groundbreaking SMHO had expected a grand opening by late 2026, and SMHO's March 2026 letter said Summer 2026.
